outcomes.text: Explain the skeleton's functions in sport: protection, muscle attachment, movement, blood cell production, mineral storage.
Classify bones as long, short, flat or irregular and link each to its role in performance.
Name the main bones and regions of the skeleton and apply their use to sport.
Classify pivot, hinge, ball and socket and condyloid joints and how they limit movement.
Describe movements at joints: flexion, extension, adduction, abduction, rotation, circumduction, plantar-flexion, dorsi-flexion, with sporting examples.
Explain the role of ligaments and tendons in participation in sport.
Describe voluntary, involuntary and cardiac muscle and their roles in sport.
Locate the main voluntary muscles (deltoid to tibialis anterior) and state what each does.
Explain antagonistic muscle pairs creating opposing movement at joints.
Describe fast and slow twitch fibre types and their use in activities.
Explain how skeletal and muscular systems work together in sport.
Explain the cardiovascular system's functions: transport, clotting and temperature regulation.
Describe the heart's structure and its role in circulating blood during exercise.
Relate the structure of arteries, capillaries and veins to function during exercise.
Explain vasoconstriction, vasodilation and vascular shunting during exercise compared with rest.
Explain the importance of red and white blood cells, platelets and plasma in sport.
Compare inhaled and exhaled air and how exercise changes it.
Explain vital capacity, tidal volume and why tidal volume rises with exercise.
Locate the respiratory system's parts and their roles in moving oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Explain alveoli structure and gas exchange at different exercise intensities.
Explain how the cardiovascular and respiratory systems work together in sport.
Explain aerobic energy release from glucose and oxygen, and anaerobic release producing lactic acid.
Explain fats and carbohydrates as fuel sources for aerobic and anaerobic activity.

subtopics.title: Short- and long-term effects of exercise

outcomes.text: Explain short-term effects of exercise on lactate build-up and muscle fatigue.
Explain short-term effects of exercise on heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output.
Explain short-term effects of exercise on depth and rate of breathing.
Explain how breathing and circulation work together to supply muscles and aid recovery.
Relate long-term effects of exercise on body systems to section 3.4.
Interpret graphs of heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output at rest and during exercise.
Describe first, second and third class levers and their use in sport.
Explain mechanical advantage and disadvantage of the body's levers.
Describe movement using sagittal, frontal and transverse planes and frontal, sagittal and vertical axes.
Describe somersault movement in the sagittal plane about the frontal axis.
Describe cartwheel movement in the frontal plane about the sagittal axis.
Describe a full twist jump in the transverse plane about the vertical axis.
Define fitness, health, exercise and performance and explain how they relate.
Describe the components of fitness and their relative importance in sport.
Explain the purpose and protocols of fitness tests and how to choose the right test.
Collect and interpret fitness test data against normative tables.
Describe tests: Cooper, Harvard Step, Illinois agility, grip dynamometer, sit-ups, press-ups, 30 m sprint, vertical jump, sit and reach.
Relate how fitness is improved to section 3.3.
Plan training using individual needs, specificity, overload, FITT, overtraining, reversibility and training zones.
Choose training methods and intensities from fitness requirements, facilities and current level.
Describe continuous, Fartlek, circuit, interval, plyometric, resistance training and fitness classes, with pros and cons.
Describe long-term effects of aerobic and anaerobic training on muscles, bones and the heart and lungs.
Explain that training lets a performer train for longer and more intensely.
Describe long-term benefits to the muscular-skeletal system and the need for rest and recovery.
Describe long-term benefits to the cardio-respiratory system.
Use a PARQ to assess readiness for training and adjust training.
Explain how to prevent injury through training principles, rules, protective equipment and checks.
Describe common sports injuries: concussion, fractures, dislocation, sprain, torn cartilage, soft tissue injury.
Describe the RICE treatment.
Evaluate performance-enhancing drugs and their positive and negative effects.
Explain the purpose of warm-ups and cool downs.
Describe the phases of a warm-up.
Describe activities in warm-ups and cool downs.
Develop understanding of data analysis in physical activity and sport.
Explain how qualitative and quantitative data are collected in fitness and sport.
Present data in tables and graphs.
Interpret data accurately.
Analyse and evaluate your own results against normative data.
Explain how improving fitness components improves physical health.
Explain how activity improves emotional and psychological health.
Explain how activity improves social health.
Describe the positive and negative health effects of fitness on wellbeing.
Explain how designing, monitoring and evaluating a personal exercise programme promotes health.
Describe lifestyle choices: diet, activity, work/rest/sleep, alcohol and nicotine.
Explain positive and negative effects of lifestyle choices on health and fitness.
Explain the consequences of a sedentary lifestyle: obesity, heart disease, diabetes, osteoporosis.
Interpret graphs of trends in physical health issues.
Describe the nutrients and ratios of a balanced diet for health and performance.
Explain the role of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, carbohydrate loading and protein timing.
Explain the role of vitamins, minerals, water and fibre.
Describe factors affecting optimum weight: sex, height, bone structure, muscle girth.
Explain how optimum weight varies by role in different sports.
Explain the energy balance for a healthy weight.
Explain why hydration matters and how to maintain it.
Classify skills on the open-closed, basic-complex and low-high organisation continua.
Describe massed, distributed, fixed and variable practice.
Choose the most relevant practice for developing different skills.
Explain how goal setting improves performance.
Explain the SMART principles and the value of each.
Set and review targets to improve performance.
Describe visual, verbal, manual and mechanical guidance.
Evaluate each type of guidance for different performers and contexts.
Describe intrinsic, extrinsic, concurrent and terminal feedback.
Interpret graphs of data on feedback and performance.
Describe mental preparation: warm up and mental rehearsal.
Describe how gender, age, socio-economic group, ethnicity and disability affect participation rates.
Interpret graphs of participation trends.
Explain the relationship between commercialisation, the media and sport.
Evaluate commercialisation and the media for sponsors, sports, performers and spectators.
Interpret graphs of trends in commercialisation of sport.
Describe sportsmanship, gamesmanship and deviance at elite level, with reasons and consequences.
Interpret graphs of trends in ethical and socio-cultural issues in sport.
Develop understanding of data analysis in physical activity and sport.
Explain how qualitative and quantitative data are collected in fitness and sport.
Present data in tables and graphs.
Interpret data accurately.
Analyse and evaluate your own results against normative data.
